reach.rationale: No experimental APIs at all, but two APIs that graduated to stable only in v22 (~5 months ago) — resource() and @Service() — sit in the central data layer of every page. This is exactly 'recently-stable APIs in central places'.

evidence: app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:15-22 — all HTTP + in-memory caching funnels through one @Service()
app/src/app/core/pokedex-data.ts — second service encapsulates domain fetching
app/src/app/pages/type-page.ts:97, type-list-page.ts:33, ability-page.ts:65 — identical params/loader pattern at each resource() call site
containment.rationale: resource() call sites span five page files (not one wrapper), but every loader goes through the two services, and the usage pattern is uniform enough that a migration would be mechanical. Nothing else experimental to contain.

evidence: app/src/app/pages/home-page.ts:135-160 — resource params() reacts to input-bound query params, replacing manual switchMap plumbing; spec requires URL-driven filters
app/src/app/pages/pokemon-page.ts:273-277 — second resource derives from the first via params returning undefined until ready
app/src/app/pages/home-page.ts:196-199 — effect() mirrors resource into a view signal to keep stale content during refetch; mild indirection
app/src/app/app.config.ts:11 — withComponentInputBinding pairs route query with signals, long-stable choice over the dev-preview Router resources
justification.rationale: Every recently-stable API buys something concrete: reactive refetch on URL params, built-in loading/error state, and a centralized caching service; @Service() is the current officially recommended pattern. Not quite perfect because @Service is partly stylistic and the home page's effect-mirror adds a small hand-rolled state layer.

findings.issue: effect() copies resource().value() into a separate view signal, a hand-rolled keep-last-value layer
findings.suggestion: Document why (retaining the previous page during refetch) or rely on resource's value()/status directly if the flicker is acceptable

findings.issue: @angular/forms is declared as a dependency but never imported; forms are native elements handled manually
findings.suggestion: Drop the unused dependency (or adopt the now-stable Signal Forms if form logic grows)

findings.issue: "experimentalDecorators": true reads as an experiment flag but is the standard TS compiler option Angular decorators require
findings.suggestion: No action needed; just noting it is not a framework-level experimental feature

summary: This is a stable-only Angular 22 app: zero experimental, preview or canary APIs, with the recently-stabilized resource() and @Service() APIs (both graduated in v22, June 2026) carrying the data layer. Those uses are justified, idiomatic and centralized behind two services, so residual risk is limited to the APIs being barely six months into stability. The app deliberately avoids every still-experimental v22 feature (@boundary, Router resources, MCP tools).
